Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/robots/osudrl__cassie-mujoco-sim --backend fake (exit 0; evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). The last run had G1-G9 pass with no finding and no warning, and G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY citation. Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017 (run wC-093) and reviewed_by stays null; no human reviewed or tested the package, no hardware was attached, no hardware backend exists and no hardware run is claimed. The loader refusal of an unreviewed model-written hardware backend applies only at R2 and R3; this package is simulated R0 and declares no hardware backend.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card says decision family-config, family mujoco and helper MujocoDriver, but the upstream entry symbol is the ctypes class cassiemujoco:CassieSim (confirmed at example/cassiemujoco.py:31), not the mujoco Python module. The mujoco package is not installed and the card's install block is empty; a MujocoDriver would load the MJCF through that missing module and could not name CassieSim as native (the card's entry symbol is an override, and G7 requires native to be that symbol). This package is therefore a decorated direct Driver over CassieSim with a package fake. It calls CassieSim.step_pd for cap.world.step.v1 and CassieSim.full_reset plus CassieSim.set_time for cap.world.reset.v1. The entry symbol's file is example/cassiemujoco.py; cassiemujoco is its import name in that directory.

MOCK PATH: the card prefers upstream-sim, but the upstream simulator is the ctypes wrapper over libcassiemujoco.so and MuJoCo 2.10 (Makefile:5, include/cassiemujoco.h:110-190); it is not installed by the card, and package code may not import, build or run the clone. fake.py is the package's own pure Python stand-in with exactly the public CassieSim methods the driver calls (step_pd, full_reset, time, timestep, qpos, qvel, ctrl, set_time, set_qpos, set_qvel, set_ctrl); every number in it is placeholder test data marked # placeholder. It was not compared with the upstream library.

COVERAGE: reads time_ms, qpos (35 entries), qvel (32), ctrl (10), tick, timestep_ms and seed; cap.world.step.v1 takes ticks and an optional action {ctrl: [10]} bounded element-wise by the ten actuator_ctrlrange values of model/cassie.xml:258-267; cap.world.reset.v1 calls full_reset, sets the time to zero and records the supplied seed as a label. The fidelity says reset is partial because full_reset does not clear MuJoCo's warm-start accelerations or the simulator time (the driver sets the time), determinism is none because no full snapshot exists, and engine mujoco/F1 describes the upstream model, not the fake.

NOT COVERED: the real MuJoCo physics in the fake (no contacts, gravity, torque-speed limit, state estimator or sensor model; its inertia and step response are placeholder test data), the pd_in_t task-level and per-motor target and gain inputs, the UDP physical-Cassie path (CassieUdp), snapshots and restore, and a hardware backend (none exists). The qpos/qvel/ctrl arrays are returned at the full model sizes, not reduced. No catalogue_requests: only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 are used, and both bind resource kind world.sim. fixtures/conformance.json holds valid, alternate and out-of-envelope test inputs, not device facts. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed.
